Normal's hardware runs the most memory-bound parts of large-model inference inside memory itself, rather than shuttling weights to a processor. The software that makes this programmable doesn't exist yet in any standard form. Getting a model correct on that hardware is the frontend's job; making it fast is yours. As a Compiler Engineer focused on the backend, you will help design and build the custom compilation that maps LLM inference onto it, from scheduling and memory planning to the code our hardware actually executes.



You will work at the boundary between the compiler and the hardware, closely enough to know when an optimization belongs at a different layer, or when the right answer is a new abstraction. Our chip is pre-silicon, so you will measure your work against our simulators and FPGA prototypes first, and against silicon as it arrives.
